title: A rules file and its why file

record.path: <name>-WHY.md beside the rules file it explains (AGENTS-WHY.md for AGENTS.md)

codes.means: the why file names no standard, the bare unversioned rules URL, or another kind's standard
the why file names a version of the rules standard this validator does not implement
codes.fix: install the rules-md version that implements it, or rewrite the header to https://hypercontext.wiki/standards/rules/v1

codes.means: kind is missing or is not "rules"
codes.fix: set kind: rules in the why file's header

codes.means: the header names no rules_file, or the file it names is not there, so nothing can be checked against it
codes.fix: set rules_file to the rules file's path, relative to the why file

codes.means: a marker's id is not a lowercase slug of at most 48 characters
codes.fix: use letters, digits and single hyphens (git-pathspec); give a new id rather than renaming an old one

codes.means: two markers in the rules file carry the same id, so a citation cannot say which rule it means
codes.fix: give the second rule its own id, or merge the two rules

codes.means: a rule has no section in the why file, so nobody can look up why it exists
codes.fix: add a ## <id> section with status: live and the story; rules-md add-missing --apply scaffolds one

codes.means: two why sections carry the same id
a why section is live but no rule carries its id, so the rule was deleted or renamed without being retired
codes.fix: restore the rule, or set status: retired with replaced_by naming what took its place

codes.means: a rule marked retired in the why file is still in the rules file
codes.fix: remove the rule from the rules file, or set it back to status: live

codes.means: a retired rule does not say what replaced it
codes.fix: set replaced_by to the rule id, hook or skill that took its place, or none

codes.means: status is not live or retired
codes.fix: set status: live or status: retired

codes.means: a live why section records no fingerprint of its rule, so a rewording cannot be noticed
codes.fix: read the rule and its story, then run rules-md stamp --id <id> --apply

codes.means: the rule's words changed after its why section was last read against them
codes.fix: read the why section against the new wording, fix whichever is wrong, then rules-md stamp --id <id> --apply

codes.means: an earned date is not a real date written YYYY-MM-DD
codes.fix: write each date YYYY-MM-DD, comma separated
